description: Issue #838 AC5: `ol-duplicate-definition` (`spec/grammar.md:416`, `spec/error-model.md:126`). A name the program -- or a library written in OpenLogo -- already declares is not a name OpenLogo owns, so it gets its own code and its own message. All three collision shapes the spec names are exercised in one file, across BOTH declaration slots and in BOTH orders: `struct` then `struct` (line 2), `struct` then `define` (line 3), and `define` then `struct` (line 9). Its Core-only sibling `core-language/check/duplicate-definition-not-profile-gated` runs collision shapes with `data` ABSENT, which is the half this file cannot prove. The first declaration of each name stays clean -- "already defined" needs an earlier occurrence to compare against -- so only the later one is flagged. What makes this code notable is that it carries TWO spans: `source_span` at the later declaration and `params.original_span` at the earlier one. `spec/error-model.md:144-147` makes that required identity rather than message decoration -- "an implementation MUST supply it rather than folding the earlier location into the message text" -- because it is what lets an editor offer *jump to the first definition*, and what makes the code work unchanged when the earlier declaration arrives from an imported module under the Modules profile. `"check": true` -- a checker rule, nothing is executed and no events are produced.
